    34	/-! ## Cocycle-A helpers for `exists_tensorObj_inverse`
    35	
    36	`trivialisation_restrict_compat` reduces the sectionwise overlap equation
    37	(residual-A step 1) from the `(U i).ι⁻¹`-vs-`(U j).ι⁻¹` form to a single-open-`V`
    38	equation, enabling `tensorObj_unit_self_duality_collapse` to close the `g·g⁻¹ = 1`
    39	cancellation (step 2). -/
    40	
    41	/-- **Reindexing iso `ρ_A` (the keystone identification).** For the chart `j : V ⟶ U` with
    42	`j ≫ U.ι = V.ι`, the `V`-restriction of an `X`-module `A` is canonically the `j`-restriction of its
    43	`U`-restriction: `A.restrict V.ι ≅ (A.restrict U.ι).restrict j`.  Built from the keystone
    44	`restrictFunctorComp j U.ι` (`Mathlib`) post-composed with the `j ≫ U.ι = V.ι` congruence
    45	`restrictFunctorCongr`.  This is the `ρ` of the blueprint S2–S4c squares, on both flanks of each. -/
    46	noncomputable def restrictCompReindex {X : Scheme.{u}} {U V : X.Opens}
    47	    (j : (V : Scheme) ⟶ (U : Scheme)) [IsOpenImmersion j] (hjι : j ≫ U.ι = V.ι) (A : X.Modules) :
    48	    A.restrict V.ι ≅ (A.restrict U.ι).restrict j :=
    49	  (restrictFunctorCongr hjι).symm.app A ≪≫ (restrictFunctorComp j U.ι).app A

    51	/-! ### Step A — atomic per-leg conjugate computations for the B2 telescope
    52	
    53	The natural-transformation identity `hNat` of `restrictFunctorIsoPullback_comp_compat_hom`
    54	is proved by conjugating both sides onto the common right adjoint `pushforward V.ι` and
    55	distributing leg-by-leg via `conjugateEquiv_comp`.  Each per-leg conjugate value is one of
    56	the following atomic claims (blueprint `lem:conjugateequiv_*`). -/
    57	
    58	/-- **c₅ (blueprint `lem:conjugateequiv_pullbackcomp_hom`): conjugate of the pullback-composition
    59	hom.** Mirror of Mathlib's `conjugateEquiv_pullbackComp_inv`: applying `conjugateEquiv` (in the
    60	swapped adjunction order, so it accepts `.hom : L₁ ⟶ L₂`) to `(pullbackComp f g).hom` gives the
    61	*inverse* of the pushforward-composition iso.  Obtained from `conjugateEquiv_pullbackComp_inv` by
    62	the `conjugateEquiv_comm` cancellation `hom ; inv = 𝟙`. -/
    63	lemma conjugateEquiv_pullbackComp_hom {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    64	    [IsOpenImmersion f] [IsOpenImmersion g] :
    65	    conjugateEquiv (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (f ≫ g))
    66	        ((pullbackPushforwardAdjunction g).comp (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f))
    67	        (pullbackComp f g).hom
    68	      = (pushforwardComp f g).inv := by
    69	  have hcomm := conjugateEquiv_comm
    70	    ((pullbackPushforwardAdjunction g).comp (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f))
    71	    (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (f ≫ g))
    72	    (α := (pullbackComp f g).inv) (β := (pullbackComp f g).hom)
    73	    (Iso.hom_inv_id _)
    74	  rw [conjugateEquiv_pullbackComp_inv] at hcomm
    75	  -- hcomm : (pushforwardComp f g).hom ≫ conjugateEquiv … (pullbackComp f g).hom = 𝟙
    76	  rw [← cancel_epi (pushforwardComp f g).hom, hcomm, Iso.hom_inv_id]
    77	
    78	/-- **LHS of the B2 telescope: the conjugate of `restrictFunctorIsoPullback f` is the identity.**
    79	`restrictFunctorIsoPullback f = leftAdjointUniq (restrictAdjunction f) (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f)`,
    80	both adjoint to the common `pushforward f`; the conjugate of a `leftAdjointUniq` hom onto the shared
    81	right adjoint is the identity. -/
    82	lemma conjugateEquiv_restrictFunctorIsoPullback_hom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    83	    [IsOpenImmersion f] :
    84	    conjugateEquiv (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f) (restrictAdjunction f)
    85	        (restrictFunctorIsoPullback f).hom
    86	      = 𝟙 (pushforward f) := by
    87	  rw [Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply]
    88	  simp only [restrictFunctorIsoPullback, Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq, Iso.symm_hom,
    89	    conjugateIsoEquiv_symm_apply_inv, Iso.refl_inv]
    90	
    91	/-- **c₃ (blueprint `lem:conjugateequiv_restrictfunctorisopullback_whiskerright`): conjugate of the
    92	`f`-comparison whiskered by `restrict j`.** The leg `whiskerRight (restrictFunctorIsoPullback f).hom
    93	(restrictFunctor j)`, conjugated through the composite adjunctions `(pPA f).comp (rA j) →
    94	(rA f).comp (rA j)`, is the identity: by `conjugateEquiv_whiskerRight` it becomes
    95	`whiskerLeft (pushforward j)` of the (identity) conjugate of `restrictFunctorIsoPullback f`. -/
    96	lemma conjugateEquiv_restrictFunctorIsoPullback_whiskerRight {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    97	    (f : Y ⟶ X) (j : Z ⟶ Y) [IsOpenImmersion f] [IsOpenImmersion j] :
    98	    conjugateEquiv ((pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).comp (restrictAdjunction j))
    99	        ((restrictAdjunction f).comp (restrictAdjunction j))
   100	        (Functor.whiskerRight (restrictFunctorIsoPullback f).hom (restrictFunctor j))
   101	      = 𝟙 _ := by
   102	  rw [conjugateEquiv_whiskerRight, conjugateEquiv_restrictFunctorIsoPullback_hom,
   103	    Functor.whiskerLeft_id']
   104	
   105	/-- **c₄ (blueprint `lem:conjugateequiv_restrictfunctorisopullback_whiskerleft`): conjugate of the
   106	`j`-comparison whiskered into `pullback f`.** The leg `whiskerLeft (pullback f)
   107	(restrictFunctorIsoPullback j).hom`, conjugated through `(pPA f).comp (pPA j) → (pPA f).comp (rA j)`,
   108	is the identity: by `conjugateEquiv_whiskerLeft` it becomes `whiskerRight` of the (identity)
   109	conjugate of `restrictFunctorIsoPullback j`. -/
   110	lemma conjugateEquiv_restrictFunctorIsoPullback_whiskerLeft {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
   111	    (f : Y ⟶ X) (j : Z ⟶ Y) [IsOpenImmersion f] [IsOpenImmersion j] :
   112	    conjugateEquiv ((pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).comp (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction j))
   113	        ((pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).comp (restrictAdjunction j))
   114	        (Functor.whiskerLeft (pullback f) (restrictFunctorIsoPullback j).hom)
   115	      = 𝟙 _ := by
   116	  rw [conjugateEquiv_whiskerLeft, conjugateEquiv_restrictFunctorIsoPullback_hom,
   117	    Functor.whiskerRight_id']
   118	
   119	/-- Sectionwise value of `(restrictFunctor f).map`: pushforward along an open immersion acts on a
   120	morphism `φ` by reindexing its components through `f ''ᵁ -`.  Holds by `rfl`; project-local because
   121	it is only used to drive the sectionwise reduction in
   122	`conjugateEquiv_restrictFunctorComp_inv`. -/
   123	private lemma restrictFunctor_map_app' {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsOpenImmersion f]
   124	    {M N : Y.Modules} (φ : M ⟶ N) (U : X.Opens) :
   125	    ((restrictFunctor f).map φ).app U = φ.app (f ''ᵁ U) := rfl
   126	
   127	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
   128	-- The sectionwise reduction below traverses the `SheafOfModules.pushforward` carrier diamond
   129	-- (`restrict_map`/`erw` past defeq-not-syntactic `≫`), which needs a raised heartbeat budget.
   130	set_option linter.unusedTactic false in
   131	set_option linter.unreachableTactic false in
   132	/-- **Restrict-side conjugate of the restriction-composition isomorphism.**
   133	The conjugate of `(restrictFunctorComp f g).hom` across the composite restrict-adjunction equals
   134	`(pushforwardComp f g).hom`.  Public so the terminal file can consume it.  (Ported from the v4.30
   135	root `TensorObjSubstrate.lean` tail, which was dropped in the file-split migration.) -/
   136	lemma conjugateEquiv_restrictFunctorComp_inv {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
   137	    [IsOpenImmersion f] [IsOpenImmersion g] :
   138	    conjugateEquiv ((restrictAdjunction g).comp (restrictAdjunction f))
   139	        (restrictAdjunction (f ≫ g)) (restrictFunctorComp f g).hom
   140	      = (pushforwardComp f g).hom := by
   141	  rw [show (restrictFunctorComp f g).hom
   142	      = (Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso (restrictAdjunction g) (restrictAdjunction f)
   143	          (restrictAdjunction (f ≫ g)) (pushforwardComp f g)).inv from ?_]
   144	  · exact Adjunction.conjugateEquiv_leftAdjointCompIso_inv _ _ _ _
   145	  · ext M U : 3
   146	    rw [restrictFunctorComp_hom_app_app]
   147	    simp only [Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso, conjugateIsoEquiv_symm_apply_inv,
   148	      Iso.symm_inv, conjugateEquiv_symm_apply_app, Adjunction.comp_unit_app, Hom.comp_app,
   149	      restrictFunctor_map_app', pushforwardComp_hom_app_app]
   150	    erw [Hom.comp_app, restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app, pushforward_map_app,
   151	      restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app, restrictAdjunction_counit_app_app]
   152	    simp only [Functor.comp_obj, restrict_map]
   153	    erw [Category.id_comp, ← M.presheaf.map_comp, ← M.presheaf.map_comp]
   154	    all_goals first
   155	      | rfl
   156	      | (congr 1; exact Subsingleton.elim _ _)
   157	
   158	/-- **General B2 (`.hom`/NatTrans level): `restrictFunctorIsoPullback` pseudonaturality across a
   159	LITERAL composite `f ≫ g`.**  The dual-flank analogue of `restrictFunctorIsoPullback_comp_compat_hom`
   160	for general composable open immersions `f : Z ⟶ Y`, `g : Y ⟶ X` (arbitrary schemes), with NO
   161	`restrictFunctorCongr`/`pullbackCongr` congruence legs (the composite is literal, so those collapse).
   162	Same conjugate-telescope proof: `conjugateEquiv` injectivity onto `pushforward (f ≫ g)`, distribute
   163	leg-by-leg via `← conjugateEquiv_comp`, then the keystone `conjugateEquiv_restrictFunctorComp_inv`
   164	(c₂ ↦ `(pushforwardComp).hom`) + `conjugateEquiv_pullbackComp_hom` (c₅ ↦ `(pushforwardComp).inv`)
   165	+ the two whisker-conjugates (c₃/c₄ ↦ 𝟙) telescope to `𝟙`. -/
   166	private lemma restrictFunctorIsoPullback_comp_general_hom {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : Z ⟶ Y)
   167	    (g : Y ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion f] [IsOpenImmersion g] (A : X.Modules) :
   168	    (restrictFunctorIsoPullback (f ≫ g)).hom.app A
   169	      = (restrictFunctorComp f g).hom.app A
   170	          ≫ (restrictFunctor f).map ((restrictFunctorIsoPullback g).hom.app A)
   171	          ≫ (restrictFunctorIsoPullback f).hom.app ((pullback g).obj A)
   172	          ≫ (pullbackComp f g).hom.app A := by
   173	  -- Same leg-by-leg conjugate telescope as the chart version `restrictFunctorIsoPullback_comp_compat_hom`,
   174	  -- but for the LITERAL composite `f ≫ g` (no `restrictFunctorCongr`/`pullbackCongr` flank legs, so
   175	  -- only the 4 inner legs survive and they telescope directly to `𝟙`).
   176	  have hNat : (restrictFunctorIsoPullback (f ≫ g)).hom
   177	      = (restrictFunctorComp f g).hom
   178	          ≫ Functor.whiskerRight (restrictFunctorIsoPullback g).hom (restrictFunctor f)
   179	          ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft (pullback g) (restrictFunctorIsoPullback f).hom
   180	          ≫ (pullbackComp f g).hom := by
   181	    apply (conjugateEquiv (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (f ≫ g))
   182	      (restrictAdjunction (f ≫ g))).injective
   183	    rw [conjugateEquiv_restrictFunctorIsoPullback_hom]
   184	    rw [← conjugateEquiv_comp (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (f ≫ g))
   185	          ((restrictAdjunction g).comp (restrictAdjunction f)) (restrictAdjunction (f ≫ g)),
   186	        ← conjugateEquiv_comp (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (f ≫ g))
   187	          ((pullbackPushforwardAdjunction g).comp (restrictAdjunction f))
   188	          ((restrictAdjunction g).comp (restrictAdjunction f)),
   189	        ← conjugateEquiv_comp (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (f ≫ g))
   190	          ((pullbackPushforwardAdjunction g).comp (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f))
   191	          ((pullbackPushforwardAdjunction g).comp (restrictAdjunction f))]
   192	    rw [conjugateEquiv_restrictFunctorComp_inv, conjugateEquiv_pullbackComp_hom,
   193	        conjugateEquiv_restrictFunctorIsoPullback_whiskerRight,
   194	        conjugateEquiv_restrictFunctorIsoPullback_whiskerLeft]
   195	    simp only [Category.id_comp, Category.comp_id, Iso.inv_hom_id]
   196	  have happ := congr_app hNat A
   197	  -- v4.31: `simpa using` runs at reducible transparency; normalise `happ` then close by `exact`.
   198	  simp only [NatTrans.comp_app, Functor.whiskerRight_app, Functor.whiskerLeft_app] at happ
   199	  exact happ
   200	
   201	/-- **General B2 (iso level): `restrictFunctorIsoPullback` pseudonaturality across a LITERAL
   202	composite `f ≫ g`.**  The dual-flank analogue of `restrictFunctorIsoPullback_comp_compat` for general
   203	composable open immersions, with `restrictFunctorComp f g` (NOT `restrictCompReindex`) as the head and
   204	NO `pullbackCongr` tail.  Both sides are isos `(restrictFunctor (f ≫ g)).obj A ≅ (pullback (f ≫ g)).obj A`;
   205	pinned by the `leftAdjointUniq` characterisation as in the chart version, the residual `.hom`-naturality
   206	being `restrictFunctorIsoPullback_comp_general_hom`. -/
   207	lemma restrictFunctorIsoPullback_comp_general {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : Z ⟶ Y)
   208	    (g : Y ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion f] [IsOpenImmersion g] (A : X.Modules) :
   209	    (restrictFunctorIsoPullback (f ≫ g)).app A
   210	      = (restrictFunctorComp f g).app A
   211	          ≪≫ (restrictFunctor f).mapIso ((restrictFunctorIsoPullback g).app A)
   212	          ≪≫ (restrictFunctorIsoPullback f).app ((pullback g).obj A)
   213	          ≪≫ (pullbackComp f g).app A := by
   214	  apply Iso.ext
   215	  apply (restrictAdjunction (f ≫ g)).homEquiv _ _ |>.injective
   216	  conv_lhs => rw [show ((restrictFunctorIsoPullback (f ≫ g)).app A).hom
   217	    = ((restrictAdjunction (f ≫ g)).leftAdjointUniq
   218	        (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (f ≫ g))).hom.app A
   219	    from rfl, Adjunction.homEquiv_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app]
   220	  rw [Adjunction.homEquiv_unit]
   221	  simp only [Iso.trans_hom, Functor.mapIso_hom, Functor.map_comp, Iso.app_hom]
   222	  rw [show (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (f ≫ g)).unit.app A
   223	      = (restrictAdjunction (f ≫ g)).unit.app A
   224	          ≫ (pushforward (f ≫ g)).map ((restrictFunctorIsoPullback (f ≫ g)).hom.app A)
   225	      from (Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app (restrictAdjunction (f ≫ g))
   226	        (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (f ≫ g)) A).symm]
   227	  congr 1
   228	  rw [restrictFunctorIsoPullback_comp_general_hom f g A, Functor.map_comp, Functor.map_comp,
   229	    Functor.map_comp]
   230	
   231	/-- **Unit-restriction identification.** For an open immersion `f : Y ⟶ X`, the restriction of the
   232	global unit `𝒪_X` to `Y` is `𝒪_Y`: `(𝒪_X).restrict f ≅ 𝒪_Y`.  This is `uι(f)` of the blueprint
   233	(`(restrictFunctorIsoPullback f).app 𝒪_X ≪≫ pullbackUnitIso f`); also the unit identification used
   234	on the chart-scheme side of S4a/S4b. -/
   235	noncomputable def unitRestrictIso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion f] :
   236	    restrict (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) f ≅ SheafOfModules.unit Y.ringCatSheaf :=
   237	  (restrictFunctorIsoPullback f).app (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) ≪≫ pullbackUnitIso f
   238	
   239	/-- **RFIP pseudonaturality across an equality of open immersions (naturality-square form).**
   240	For `h : f = f'`, the `restrictFunctorIsoPullback f` comparison followed by the `pullbackCongr h`
   241	reindex equals the `restrictFunctorCongr h` reindex followed by `restrictFunctorIsoPullback f'`.
   242	By `subst h` both congruences collapse to the identity. -/
   243	@[reassoc]
   244	private lemma restrictFunctorIsoPullback_congr_hom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f f' : Y ⟶ X}
   245	    [IsOpenImmersion f] [IsOpenImmersion f'] (h : f = f') (A : X.Modules) :
   246	    (restrictFunctorIsoPullback f).hom.app A ≫ (pullbackCongr h).hom.app A
   247	      = (restrictFunctorCongr h).hom.app A ≫ (restrictFunctorIsoPullback f').hom.app A := by
   248	  subst h
   249	  have hr : (restrictFunctorCongr (rfl : f = f)).hom.app A = 𝟙 _ := by
   250	    ext U; simp; rfl
   251	  have hp : (pullbackCongr (rfl : f = f)).hom.app A = 𝟙 _ := by
   252	    simp [pullbackCongr]
   253	  rw [hr, hp, Category.id_comp, Category.comp_id]
   254	
   255	/-- **Front-leg normalisation: the `hom` of `restrictFunctorCongr` along the reversed equality is the
   256	`inv` along the original.**  Both are maps `restrictFunctor f' ⟶ restrictFunctor f`; their sheaf
   257	components are the same `eqToHom`-reindex. -/
   258	private lemma restrictFunctorCongr_symm_hom_app {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f f' : Y ⟶ X}
   259	    [IsOpenImmersion f] [IsOpenImmersion f'] (h : f = f') (A : X.Modules) :
   260	    (restrictFunctorCongr h.symm).hom.app A = (restrictFunctorCongr h).inv.app A := by
   261	  ext U; simp
   262	
   263	-- The internal `Hom.resLE (𝟙 X) U V hVU` carries the `V ≤ U`-proof at the defeq-but-not-
   264	-- instances-transparency type `V ≤ (𝟙 X) ⁻¹ᵁ U`; relax the `isDefEq` transparency check so the
   265	-- `Iso.hom_inv_id_app`/naturality rewrites below match across that reindex.
   266	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
   267	/-- **Keystone Seam-1 identity: `restrictIsoUnitOfLE` is the reindexed `restrict j`-image of the
   268	trivialisation.**  For the chart `j : V ⟶ U` (`j ≫ U.ι = V.ι`) and a trivialisation
   269	`e : M|_U ≅ 𝒪_U`, the refined trivialisation `restrictIsoUnitOfLE hVU e : M|_V ≅ 𝒪_V` factors as the
   270	reindex `restrictCompReindex j hjι M`, the `restrict j`-image `(restrictFunctor j).mapIso e`, and the
   271	unit-restriction comparison `unitRestrictIso j`.  This is the `e ↦ (restrict j) e` identification the
   272	blueprint Seam-1 split rests on (`restrictIsoUnitOfLE hVU e = (restrict j) e` modulo the unit
   273	identifications).  It mirrors the definitional chart-chase of `restrictIsoUnitOfLE` itself, where the
   274	internal chart morphism is exactly `j = Scheme.Hom.resLE (𝟙 X) U V hVU`. -/
   275	lemma restrictIsoUnitOfLE_eq_restrict {X : Scheme.{u}} {M : X.Modules} {U V : X.Opens}
   276	    (hVU : V ≤ U) (j : (V : Scheme) ⟶ (U : Scheme)) [IsOpenImmersion j] (hjι : j ≫ U.ι = V.ι)
   277	    (e : M.restrict U.ι ≅ SheafOfModules.unit (U : Scheme).ringCatSheaf) :
   278	    restrictIsoUnitOfLE hVU e
   279	      = restrictCompReindex j hjι M
   280	          ≪≫ (restrictFunctor j).mapIso e
   281	          ≪≫ unitRestrictIso j := by
   282	  -- `restrictIsoUnitOfLE hVU e` (unfolded) is the pullback-world chart-chase
   283	  --   `RFIP(V.ι) ≪≫ pullbackCongr(hjι.symm) ≪≫ (pullbackComp j U.ι).symm
   284	  --      ≪≫ (pullback j)(RFIP(U.ι).symm) ≪≫ (pullback j) e ≪≫ asIso (pullbackObjUnitToUnit j)`.
   285	  -- The RHS unfolds `restrictCompReindex = (restrictFunctorCongr hjι).symm ≪≫ restrictFunctorComp j U.ι`
   286	  -- and `unitRestrictIso j = RFIP(j).app 𝒪_U ≪≫ pullbackUnitIso j`.  The two presentations agree once
   287	  -- `restrictFunctorComp`/`restrictFunctorCongr` are pushed into the pullback world by
   288	  -- `restrictFunctorIsoPullback_comp_general` (the same RFIP-bridge S2/S4c use); the trailing
   289	  -- `pullbackObjUnitToUnit j` matches `pullbackUnitIso j` definitionally.
   290	  -- After `Iso.ext` the residual goal is the `.hom`-level chart-chase reconciliation
   291	  --   `(restrictIsoUnitOfLE hVU e).hom
   292	  --      = (restrictCompReindex j hjι M ≪≫ (restrictFunctor j).mapIso e ≪≫ unitRestrictIso j).hom`.
   293	  -- BLOCKER: the `restrictFunctorComp ↔ pullbackComp` reconciliation through the `pullbackCongr`/
   294	  -- `restrictFunctorCongr` shim needs build-driven `trace_state` stepping (LSP dead on this
   295	  -- monster-importing file); re-break candidate per the no-grind guard.
   296	  -- `U.ι` is mono, so the abstract chart `j` is forced to equal the internal `Hom.resLE` used by
   297	  -- `restrictIsoUnitOfLE`; identify them so the two presentations share the same chart.
   298	  have hjeq : j = Scheme.Hom.resLE (𝟙 X) U V hVU := by
   299	    rw [← cancel_mono U.ι, hjι, Scheme.Hom.resLE_comp_ι, Category.comp_id]

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.

Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.

## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)

Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).

remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
shorter. This pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
